The script lands a stack bottom up, one pull request at a time, under the merge policy.
The forge module serves every pull request operation. Verdicts come from verifier sessions that did not write the code; the policy counts only those.
The loop lands in the order given and stops at the first pull request that does not land.
A verdict covers one head; restack keeps verdicts only where the patch-id is unchanged.
ship merges at the head the policy was checked on and reads the result back from the forge.
The pipelines are waited for through the forge flow; no watcher script.
The loop ends at the first refusal.
The script answers landed or stopped, with each pull request's outcome.
The audit script, df and chat transcripts are not carried: the workflow reads git.worktree.list for the worktrees the merged head was built in.
A worktree a session runs in is kept and named; there is no sidebar or pinned chat.
No transcripts are read: whether a session runs in a worktree is what git.worktree.list reports.
A worktree with uncommitted work is kept and named, never removed, and nothing is asked.
A clean worktree with no session is removed through git.worktree.remove; the branch stays.
Simulators, Xcode and Cursor caches and package caches are outside git and outside the workflow.
The workflow removes only worktrees that are clean and run no session.
The script answers what it removed and what it kept with the reason; it reports no df.
